newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool processor sees A$63mln sales boost.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool processor sees A$63mln sales boost.

text.p: Australia's largest wool processor, the family-owned G.H Michell and Sons Pty Ltd, said on Friday its A$10 million wool processing plant would boost export earnings by up to A$63 million a year.

South Australian Premier John Olsen, who opened the plant, said in a statement the company, now the world's third largest wool processor, exported wool to 35 countries and earned more than A$350 million a year in exports.

G.H. Michell said the new six million kilogram plant, which included a high density wool tops press, would treat wool to make it "shrinkproof" and offered other improvements to suit the trend towards more casual, easy care fabrics.
"We believe the move is one of Michell's most significant, indicating the start of a new era of wool expansion for the company," managing director John Michell said in a statement.

He said all the "superwash" processes of the plant would be linked to the company's main processing plant, providing increased opportunities for improvement in productivity, expansion of operation, and product development.
